tools.name: list_locations
tools.description: List the Square seller's locations (the IDs every other Square call is scoped by)

tools.name: list_payments
tools.description: List Square payments, optionally filtered to one location or a start time

location_id.description: Optional Square location ID to filter by (defaults to all locations the token can see)

begin_time.description: Optional RFC 3339 start timestamp, e.g. 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z (defaults to one year before end_time)

sort_order.description: Optional sort order on created_at (default DESC)

sort_field.description: Optional field to sort by (default DEFAULT, which is creation order)

tools.name: list_catalog
tools.description: List Square catalog objects (items, categories, taxes, discounts), optionally filtered by type

types.description: Optional comma-separated catalog object types, e.g. ITEM,CATEGORY,TAX,DISCOUNT,MODIFIER_LIST (default ITEM plus the other top-level types)

cursor.description: Optional pagination cursor returned by a previous call

needs_review: square_version_pinned: Square requires a Square-Version header on every request and dates its API monthly, so the version is pinned statically here (2025-01-23) rather than left to Square's default, which is the oldest version the account has used. Bumping it is a deliberate spec edit, and the probe below confirms the header is accepted (an unsupported version answers 400 BAD_REQUEST, not 401).
read_only_surface: all four tools are GET. Square's write surface (CreatePayment, CreateCustomer, catalog upsert, refunds) is deliberately excluded from this wave, so no tool carries write:true.

list_payments_no_location_default: location_id is optional. Omitted, Square returns payments across every location the access token can see; a seller with many locations should pass one from list_locations first.

catalog_list_has_no_limit: ListCatalog takes cursor and types only, with no page-size parameter, so the response is bounded by truncate 2000 rather than by a clamp. Pagination is exposed through the cursor input.
rateLimit 30/min is a local courtesy and spend guard chosen here, not a documented Square ceiling; Square's own limits are per endpoint and per application.

pick sources follow the documented response envelopes in the Square API reference (locations[], payments[], customers[], objects[]), not a live 2xx: no account was held, so the proof below covers wiring only, never payload shape.
